evidence: Implemented a Windows Tauri 2 desktop shell under apps/desktop that consumes the shared packages/download-engine Rust crate.
Implemented Tauri commands for queue listing, validated URL submission, destination selection, download controls, completed-file opening, and reveal-in-folder.
Implemented confirmation-based clipboard URL offers; detected clipboard URLs are emitted to the UI and are not automatically downloaded.
Configured the Tauri shell to load the existing accessible UI from src and added Windows MSI/NSIS bundle targets.
git diff --check completed successfully with exit code 0.
Both cargo check attempts terminated automatically at their configured 120-second and 60-second timeouts while resolving or compiling Tauri dependencies; neither produced a completed build result.
knownRisks: The Tauri crate build remains unverified because dependency resolution or compilation exceeded both bounded command timeouts.

The shared download engine currently exposes a blocking download operation without cooperative pause, resume, cancellation, or progress callbacks; the desktop adapter can represent requested states but cannot yet interrupt or resume an in-flight engine transfer reliably.

Application-restart queue restoration is not available through the current shared-engine API, so this adapter cannot restore persisted manifests until that dependency exposes discovery and resume operations.
No real DOM or Windows runtime test was completed for the user-visible desktop behavior in this workstream.
